why: The module's document buffer and the desktop's are the same EditableDocument, and the one thing that could quietly differ is the dispatch on top of it: which call an edit reaches, in what order, with which offsets. So every kind of edit is walked through one buffer here and the text after each is pinned. Both sides walk this file: the Rust test in src/tests/web_core.rs against the desktop's own buffer, and scripts/build-web.mjs against the built module. A step names its block by something the block's source contains and a splice by the text it lands after, so neither side carries a byte offset that a step above it would shift.
